{{Quote|Can you think of a better prison than one without walls? What does your species use? Cages, I suppose.|translated=1|[[Unidentified Rakatan prisoner|Ancient Rakatan prisoner]]|<ref name="KotOR" />}}
'''Mind prisons''' were technological devices of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] that were created by the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]] as a means of [[Prison/Legends|incarcerating]] criminals and other beings they considered unsavory. However, these prisons were unusual in that an individual's physical body was not caged, but rather the mind. After the Infinite Empire collapsed in [[25,200 BBY]], the reality of mind traps became lost in the obscurity of history, however the devices themselves remained intact for thousands of years, with a few of them resurfacing millennia after.

==Properties==
{{Quote|Just do not open it&hellip; that is all I can say. It represents no danger to you so long as it remains closed.|translated=1|Lurze Kesh|<ref name="KotOR" />}}
[[File:Rakprison.jpg|thumb|Rakatan Prison|220px|left|The "inside" of a Rakatan prison]]
The outward appearance of a mind prison could resemble an ordinary cargo crate,<ref name="CSWE" /> although there was at least one example that was vaguely pyramidal in shape and had small engravings of [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] visages running along its vertical faces. The "interior" of the prison was perceived as an infinite expanse of white nothingness. However, prison's interior was also known to manifest various objects, such rune-covered pillars or a bed.<ref name="KotOR" />

The prison box itself was not considered hazardous, unless improperly opened. In that instance, the individual would find their mind under the control of the prison trap and drawn inside. Often, the victim would be confronted by a long-imprisoned [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] whose only chance for escape was to take over the victim's body. One ancient [[Unidentified Rakatan prisoner|Rakatan prisoner]] asked the newcomer a series of riddles and if they were answered incorrectly, the Rakatan would inhabit the body and attempt an escape.<ref name="KotOR" />

While some mind prisons could be open only by use of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="TUR" />  some became more easily accessible over the years.<ref name="KotOR" /> A mind prison opened from outside could remain half-opened for decades, allowing the inhabitant to influence the minds of those near the prison, while still not being able to escape completely.<ref name="Thing Found Rep">{{TORcite|type=faction|[[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]]|The Thing Czerka Found|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Are my people still about? If they were, I can't see that they'd let my prison loose so easily.|translated=1|Ancient Rakatan prisoner|<ref name="KotOR" />}}
Mind prisons were invented by [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Sentience/Legends|individuals]] of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], sometime before [[25,200 BBY]],<ref name="JvS" /> as a means of [[Prison/Legends|incarcerating]] criminals of their own [[Species/Legends|species]],<ref name="KotOR" /> and other beings they considered unacceptable, such as [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]] malefactors and [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] super-[[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]].<ref name="TUR" /> The [[Time/Legends|length]] of detention varied; individuals considered to have committed exceptionally terrible crimes expected to be confined for eternity with no means of escape.<ref name="KotOR" />

In part due to [[Rakatan plague|losing their connection]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the Infinite Empire collapsed in [[25,200 BBY]], and the remaining Rakata fled to their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], where they splintered into the various tribes of the [[Rakatan Archipelago]]. A number of tribes took with them the technology of their ancestors, including mind prisons, while other devices became forgotten in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="TUR" /> Two tribes of the Rakatan Archipelago, the [[Makatak tribe|Makatak]] and [[Tulpaa tribe]]s, possessed dozens of mind prisons that could only be opened by use of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="TUR" /> 

{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
[[File:Motta1.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Motta the Hutt, an owner of a mind prison]]
In [[3956 BBY]],<ref name="KotORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] visited [[Dreshdae]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], where he was approached by [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Lurze Kesh]], a procurer of unusual goods. Kesh had recognized Revan's [[Starship/Legends|ship]], the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'', as a former [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] vessel, and assuming that Revan was a smuggler, Kesh offered Revan a job: delivering a [[Unidentified Rakatan prisoner's mind prison|mysterious box]] to Motta the Hutt in [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Revan accepted the commission, with Kesh warning the Jedi to not open the box. Driven by curiosity, Revan disregarded the Rodian's advice, and became trapped inside the coffer - an ancient mind prison. Upon entering, Revan was greeted by an [[Unidentified Rakatan prisoner|ancient Rakatan being]] who informed him that his mind was now trapped inside. However, the antediluvian had discovered a means of escape&mdash;theorizing that this was only possible due to the prison having lost its protections&mdash;and he offered to show Revan the exit if the knight was the victor in a contest of riddles. Revan bested the Rakata and went on to deliver the mind prison to Motta.<ref name="KotOR" />
{{Endgame}}

Some time later,<ref name="Date">The ''[[The Unknown Regions]]'' campaign guide doesn't give an exact date of when [[Ruthic]] lived, but the guide does say that the Rakata tribes are most likely to be encountered during the Old Republic era. Furthermore, it states that Ruthic's tribe, the [[Tulpaa tribe|Tulpaa]], is building a small-scale version of the [[Star Forge]] that was destroyed at the end of the [[Jedi Civil War]]. Therefore, it is assumed that Elder Ruthic lived in the Old Republic era after the time of Revan.</ref> [[Ruthic|Elder Ruthic]], a [[Gender/Legends|female]] Rakata priest, rose to the leadership position of the Tulpaa tribe by banishing the tribe's former leaders, and other enemies, into a mind trap. Shortly before the collapse of the Infinite Empire, the Rakata had [[Rakatan plague|lost their connection]] to the Force, however, unlike the preceding generations, Ruthic was unique in that she had an emerging bond with the Force, enabling her to make use of the technology of her ancestors. Furthermore, Ruthic gained a wise counselor from her use of mind prisons. Upon banishing opponents to a [[Tulpaa mind prison|mind prison]], a pure-[[Blood/Legends|blooded]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] named [[Raspir]] was released. Having once served [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Sith]] [[King/Legends|King]] [[Adas]] as a [[Sith sorcerer|court magician]], Raspir's proficiency with [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] [[Magic/Legends|magic]] proved beneficial to the tribe leader.<ref name="TUR" />

One [[The Imprisoned One's mind prison|mind prison]], holding the consciousness of a [[The Imprisoned One|rogue Rakata]] dreaming of galactic conquest, was long buried in the cave on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. In the years before the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]], it was found by [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]].<ref name="Last One Out">{{TORcite|type=faction|Republic|Last One Out|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref> Corporate archeologists constructed a [[Czerka Secret Weapons Division 7|secret facility]] around the Rakata cave, but lost control of it when the imprisoned's influence turned their workers into mindless drones of his will. The facility was sealed and forgotten for a few decades, until around [[3643 BBY]] various parties clashed on Tatooine in search of the artifact. As a result, [[Republic Strategic Information Service]] got new insights into the history of Rakata,<ref name="Thing Found Rep" /> while [[Imperial Reclamation Service]] managed to secure the mind prison for their studies.<ref name="Thing Found Imp" />

==Behind the scenes==
The mind prison first appeared in [[BioWare]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]], released in [[2003]], as a "mysterious box." The object is part of an optional courier mission given by [[Lurze Kesh]]; however, in order to unlock the courier mission, the player must gain access to the secret compartment within the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]''. Furthermore, the choice to open the mysterious box is optional as well. Completion of either of the aforementioned missions does not affect the player's [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] or [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] alignment.<ref name="KotOR" />

With the publication of ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' in [[2008]], the mind prison received its own entry that further described the object's properties. Moreover, the entry for Motta the Hutt seemed to indicate that the mysterious box seen in ''Knights of the Old Republic'' was only one example of a mind prison.<ref name="CSWEMotta">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', {{C|Under ''Motta the Hutt''}}</ref>

The release of ''[[The Unknown Regions]]'', a [[Wizards of the Coast]] supplement to the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]'', in [[2010]] established the existence of many mind prisons, in addition to confirming that the mind prisons had been created by the ancient Rakata before their Infinite Empire collapsed.<ref name="JvS" />

In his endnotes for ''The Unknown Regions'', co-author [[Daniel Wallace]] stated that Raspir, King Adas's former court magician, was approximately 28,000 years old, which suggested that mind prisons were, at the very least, of that age. It also suggested that mind prisons were used by King Adas and his Sith Empire. However, as these two points had not been explicitly confirmed, they were not included in the [[Star Wars Legends|official]] history of mind prisons.<ref name="Endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2010/04/endnotes-for-star-wars-unknown-regions.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for ''The Unknown Regions''}}</ref>

Mind prisons appeared in various quests of the ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', including the planetary quest chain of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], in the climax of which both Imperial and Republic players encounter the prison of [[the Imprisoned One]]. Republic players are offered a choice of handling the prison over to [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] for profit (dark side choice), or attempting to destroy it (light side choice).<ref name="Thing Found Rep" /> Imperials may also choose to destroy the prison (light side choice), or secure it for the [[Imperial Reclamation Service]] (dark side choice).<ref name="Thing Found Imp" />
